proof:
For any $p\in\operatorname{conv}A_t$, express $p$ as a convex combination of bases in $A_t$, discarding zero coefficients. Its actual $E$-fiber contains the corresponding Minkowski combination of the $E$-fibers at the chosen bases. By $d$-dimensional Brunn–Minkowski its volume to the power $1/d$ is at least the weighted average of the input volume roots, each strictly larger than $t^{1/d}$. Hence $w_p>t$. This applies to all integer points $p=r+mq$ with $q\in Q_t\cap\mathbb Z^n$, proving exactly $|Q_t\cap\mathbb Z^n|=N_t$. It also applies to $p=r+q$ for each $q\in mQ_t\cap\mathbb Z^n$. These latter bases are distinct and belong to the actual strict level, which may have other members. The Ehrhart lower bound applies since $Q_t$ is a lattice polytope of affine dimension $s_t$ and has $N_t$ lattice points. Finite layer cake over the actual integer fibers gives the integral estimates.

At $m=2$, the difference from $2N-1$ is zero for $s=0$ and equals $(s-1)(N-(s+2)/2)\ge0$ for $s\ge1$, since $N\ge s+1$. Integration gives the stated peak correction. In the interval product, all measured volumes equal $|K|$ and the zero residue class has $N$ sites, with $m(N-1)+1$ in the whole interval. In the simplex product, the residue class contains exactly the $s+1$ scaled vertices, so $Q_t=\Delta_s$ for $0<t<|K|$. The nonnegative integer coordinates in $m\Delta_s$ sum to at most $m$ and hence have cardinality $\binom{m+s}{s}$ by adding one slack coordinate. These counts prove the equalities. Additional base coordinates can be fixed at zero, or given an interval of length less than one with zero its only integer point, with the same counts.
statement:
Let $E\subset\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$ be compact convex with $d\ge1$, let $r\in\mathbb Z^n$ and let $m\ge2$ be an integer. Write $w_p=\operatorname{vol}_d(E_p)$, $\mu(E)=\sum_{p\in\mathbb Z^n}w_p$, $A_t=\{p\in r+m\mathbb Z^n:w_p>t\}$, and $a_r=\max_{p\in r+m\mathbb Z^n}w_p$ with empty maximum zero. For $0<t<a_r$ put $N_t=|A_t|$, $s_t=\dim\operatorname{aff}A_t$ and $Q_t=\operatorname{conv}((A_t-r)/m)$. Then
$$
|Q_t\cap\mathbb Z^n|=N_t,\qquad
\big|\{p\in\mathbb Z^n:w_p>t\}\big|\ge |mQ_t\cap\mathbb Z^n|\ge B_m(s_t,N_t),
$$
where $B_m(s,N)=\binom{m+s}{s}+(N-s-1)\binom{m+s-1}{s}$. Consequently
$$
\mu(E)\ge\int_0^{a_r}|mQ_t\cap\mathbb Z^n|\,dt\ge\int_0^{a_r} B_m(s_t,N_t)\,dt.
$$
The integrals are zero when $a_r=0$. At $m=2$, the integrand $B_2(s,N)=(s+1)N-s(s+1)/2$ is at least $2N-1$, giving $\mu(E)\ge 2\sum_{p\in r+2\mathbb Z^n}w_p-a_r$. With $r=0$, both integral inequalities are equalities for $E=[0,m(N-1)]\times K$ with $N\ge2$ and for $E=(m\Delta_s)\times K$, where $K$ is a $d$-dimensional convex body and $\Delta_s$ the standard unimodular simplex in its integer coordinates. The inequalities apply to $E=C\cap H$ for any compact convex $C$ and closed ambient halfspace $H$.
title: Dimension-stratified residue-level expansion for actual mixed caps
